Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply with the bat. The umpires and players are out in the middle. Tanzid Hasan and skipper Litton Das are the openers for Bangladesh. Nuwan Thushara has the new ball and is raring to go. Off we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Kamindu Mendis offered little resistance with the bat, but couldn't stay for long as well. But when pace was on, the batters did look at some ease, but surely the pace-offs worked. Dasun Shanaka kept fighting till the end, and then came the final over thrust from the veteran, which helped Sri Lanka cross 130-run mark, which once looked a bridge too far. Well then, 133 is the magic number for Bangladesh to register their first-ever series win against Sri Lanka. However, they will be aware of the fact that Sri Lanka, too, has spin options aplenty with as many as four in the ranks. With the Bangladeshi top order not in that great touch, the early phase becomes crucial for the Lankans to dominate. Come what may, it is shaping up to be a gripping chase. Back in a bit for that. Stay tuned.

The surface offered no favors, with the ball holding up just enough to frustrate batters trying to time their strokes. On top of that, the fielders put themselves on the line with Bangladesh continuing to press in the middle phase. Rishad Hossain was central to the spin choke, keeping things miserly with great discipline, and Shamim Hossain also provided solid support to maintain that choke. Of a total 10 overs of spin, Bangladesh just conceded 41 runs, with only 54 runs coming in that 7-15 over phase, putting the chokehold on. The important feature of this was that the spinners just didn't leave the line of the stumps.

Pathum Nissanka was the lone warrior in a faltering top order, and the only one among the first five to cross into double digits. He did try to go on the offensive, but couldn’t offset the mounting pressure, though, especially with Mahedi Hasan swinging the momentum in Bangladesh’s favor. Introduced as a tactical wildcard, Mahedi Hasan delivered gold and wrapped up his spell with an ice-cold 4-1-11-4, making Sri Lanka fight tooth and nail for every run.

Bangladesh hit the ground running early doors. Their bowlers rattled Sri Lanka’s top order with a relentless assault. Chaos brewed early with a missed run out and a couple of dropped catches. But as soon as both Kusals were back in the pavilion without denting the scoreboard, the collapse began. Chandimal followed not long after, all departing in single digits, and the hosts limped to just 40/3 by the end of the Powerplay. That phase saw only two boundaries, which was clear evidence of Bangladesh's stranglehold.

A brilliant finish to the innings from the Sri Lankan veteran, Dasun Shanaka. This is not just the first time he has bailed his team out of trouble. But even after his blistering knock, Sri Lanka couldn't get past the average first innings score at the R. Premadasa, which is in the immediate north of 140. It was due to some really disciplined and controlled bowling from the Bangladeshi spinners. Just three overs went past double figures, which shows how difficult batting looked against them.

Shanaka looks to drive but misses. The ball is just inside the wide guideline and it will be an anticlimactic finish. SRI LANKA FINISH ON 132/7!

Good-length on the leg stump line. Pathum Nissanka nudges it off the back foot to deep mid-wicket for a single. 8 from that over, 14 from the last two for Sri Lanka.

Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Mustafizur Rahman to Pathum Nissanka, No run.

Two fielders converge, from point and cover, almost leading to a miscommunication. There is absolutely no calling but eventually, the fielder from cover backs off and Jaker Ali takes a simple catch. Chandimal departs for 4 (5) and Sri Lanka are 34/3 after 4.3 overs!

This one nips away from the leg stump, on a shortish length. Pathum Nissanka plays it late from the crease and glides the ball to the widish deep third region. Deep backward point cuts it off to his left and the batters get a single
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mustafizur Rahman to Pathum Nissanka, 1 run.

The fielder from point is quick to get to the ball and overthrows at the striker's end, and with no proper back up, the ball rolls through square leg, allowing the batters to cross over. It's all happening out there.

Lands full and outside off, Dinesh Chandimal flashes and flashes very hard at it hard, but only manages to get a thick outside edge which flies to the left of short third. Mustafizur Rahman stationed there flings himself towards the ball but does not manage to cling on the catch. A single taken.

Pathum tries to pull the ball which is going away from him and miscues it. Gets more height than distance, but because this is the Powerplay, manages to clear the infield. Or maybe not. Initially, it seems like the ball will land safely but Tanzim Hasan Sakib does really well to race after the ball from mid-wicket. Gets to the ball, doing all the hard work, but having got there, cannot hang on! Another brace taken.

Two more runs taken.

Commentary.Commentary: So close! Had Nissanka not dived, it would have been curtains for him. Tossed up on middle and full, Dinesh Chandimal leans on and flicks it with the spin to deep mid-wicket. They run the first one hard and push harder for the second run as well. But the throw from the deep is flat and towards the bowling end. Pathum Nissanka skates off to get to the other end to complete the double, and has to put in a full-stretch dive. Hasan collects the ball on the bounce and whips the bails off. There is an appeal for a run out and Bangladesh start to celebrate, with the umpire referring this to the third umpire. But the replay shows that Nissanka's dive has saved him.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Mahedi Hasan to Dinesh Chandimal, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: And do we have a run out? To the naked eye, that looked safe. It has been referred upstairs. Yes, the dive saves Nissanka.
Dinesh Chandimal walks in next, at number 4, replacing Kusal Perera.

Drifts into the off stump line and it turns away after pitching. Kusal Perera does not commit on the front foot and plays it away from the body, trying to push at it. Hence, gets an outside edge and it lobs straight to the first slip fielder as Tanzid Hasan takes a safe catch. Another Kusal departs and Sri Lanka are in early trouble - 19/2.

Full, outside off, hint of away swing, left alone.

Commentary.Commentary: The players are making their way out to the middle. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the openers for Sri Lanka. Shoriful Islam has the new ball for Bangladesh. Nissanka to face. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Now, time to look at the deck. Former Sri Lankan allrounder, is inspecting the deck. Maharoof feels that the pitch looks perfect. Reckons that underneath, it feels a bit dark in colour. Opines that maybe, it is because of a bit of moisture generated from watering the deck last evening and this morning. Feels that the ball might just hold onto the bat initially. Informs that the average score of 160-165 in the first innings is a winning score. Reckons that batting first is a good option. Ends by saying that spinners will come into play in the middle overs, so whoever does well in the middle overs will win the game.

The captain of Bangladesh, LITTON DAS, feels that the pitch should stay the same throughout the match. On the last game, Litton says that the feeling is good as Bangladesh needed to win that game. Adds that the win gives them a bit of confidence ahead of this clash. On the team news, Das says that Bangladesh have made two changes as well. Reminds us that Mahedi Hasan is back into the side after a long time, replacing Mohammad Saifuddin while the other change is Tanzim Hasan Sakib replacing Mehidy Hasan Miraz.

The skipper of Sri Lanka, CHARITH ASALANKA, says that he wants to bat first because he wants to put a good score on the board and defend it. On the last game, Asalanka admits that it was a big defeat from the Lankan point of view. So, wants to get back to the drawing board and iron out all issues. On the team news, Charith says that Sri Lanka are going in with two changes - with Dinesh Chandimal and Kamindu Mendis slotting in.

Really confused, as a reader, what to make about the forecast and the toss decision. Clearly, Asalanka has looked at the surface and not the heavens, because one cannot predict the future. If there is rain forecast, then the logical decision would be to chase but what if it does not rain at all? On the other hand, looking at the team composition of both sides, a bit intriguing to see the difference - Sri Lanka have gone in with 3 seamers and 4 possible spin options, while Bangladesh have gone in with 3 pacers and 3 spinning options. In short, shall we say, we could expect a lot of spin this evening.

Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tanzid Hasan, Parvez Hossain Emon, Litton Das (C and WK), Tawhid Hridoy, Shamim Hossain, Jaker Ali, Rishad Hossain, Mustafizur Rahman, Shoriful Islam, Tanzim Hasan Sakib (In for Mehidy Hasan Miraz) and Mahedi Hasan (In for Mohammad Saifuddin).

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Kusal Perera, Dinesh Chandimal (In for Avishka Fernando), Charith Asalanka (C), Dasun Shanaka, Kamindu Mendis (In for Chamika Karunaratne), Jeffrey Vandersay, Maheesh Theekshana, Binura Fernando and Nuwan Thushara.
TOSS UPDATE - Sri Lanka have won the toss and elected to BAT first.

The R. Premadasa Stadium hasn't hosted a T20I between these sides since 2018, but when it comes to this venue, Bangladesh actually hold a surprising advantage. In the four T20I matches played at Khettarama, the visitors have emerged victorious three times, giving them both momentum and positive memories as they chase that elusive series win. A nail-biting series finale is on the cards, folks! There's a bit of a weather concern as well, as the forecast suggests rain with thunderstorms. Let's just hope that this series finale doesn't end in a bummer. Stay tuned.

This marks the first time these two sides are playing a three-match T20I series on Sri Lankan soil. Their T20I history here is quite brief. Sri Lanka took the honors in the Only T20I back in 2012, while their two-match series in 2016 ended all square. Bangladesh have never managed to win a T20I series against Sri Lanka, whether home or away, making this opportunity to create history even more significant.

Bangladesh's bowling has been their standout feature throughout this series. Rishad Hossain has really found his rhythm, while the pace attack has clicked as a unit. Captain Litton Das returning to form couldn't have come at a better time and could prove crucial for their chances. They've shown they can compete with the hosts and it's just about delivering that knockout blow kind of a performance when it matters most.

The hosts suffered their heaviest T20I defeat by run margin in the second match and will be desperate not to let their home advantage slip away. Having chased in both games with mixed results, they will be looking to bounce back just like they did in the ODI series, where they recovered from a second-game loss to seal the decider. While the top order has shown decent form, the middle order has struggled, or rather, hasn't had many chances. Their Powerplay bowling has been decent, with them at least picking up two wickets on both occasions, but in Hasaranga's absence, they are certainly missing that bite in the spin department, with Maheesh Theekshana being the spearhead.

Throughout this series, Sri Lanka and Bangladesh have brought the high-octane cricket that fans crave in this intense subcontinental rivalry. Sri Lanka took the Test and ODI honours, but Bangladesh responded at every turn. They leveled the ODIs, but they couldn’t land the last blow. And now, producing a commanding second T20I win to square the series at 1-1, that victory, which was the visitors' second-biggest T20I win, hands Bangladesh a golden chance to seal its first series triumph of the tour. Yet, a Sri Lankan side in peak form on home soil will make sure they have to fight for every run.

Welcome to the decider at Khettarama! This all-format series began on the picturesque shores of Galle and has taken us across the length and breadth of Sri Lanka, now reaching its thrilling conclusion here in the capital city. Hello and welcome to our coverage for the third and final T20I between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh at the iconic R. Premadasa Stadium in Colombo.
... MATCH DAY ...

It's time for the decider in this 3-game T20 series between Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. The scoreline stands at 1-1, and the final game of the series promises to be one heck of a contest. These two sides have had some fierce games in the past, raising the temperature in both camps, and the upcoming game promises to be yet another fiery contest. After the hosts, Sri Lanka, registered a comfortable win in the 1st game of the series, the visitors came back storming in the 2nd game as they won it by a record margin. Talking about Sri Lanka, in their batting, Pathum Nissanka has been in top nick, having scored two 30-plus scores in the series. His opening partner, Kusal Mendis, too, has been in good touch, having bagged the man of the match in the first game with a blistering 73. In the first game, the two Sri Lankan openers scored more than 50% of the target runs, and hence the middle and lower order didn’t have much to contribute. Whereas, in the 2nd game, except for Pathum Nissanka, none of the batters in the top 5 crossed the 10-run mark. So in a way, the middle and lower order haven’t gotten much game time, and in a crunch game, they would want the likes of Charith Asalanka, Kusal Perera, and Avishka Fernando to fire. On the bowling front, the pace duo of Binura Fernando and Nuwan Thushara have done a decent job, as they have been fairly economical in the two games. The spin duo of Maheesh Theekshana and Jeffrey Vandersay have each delivered a decent performance in one of the two games. For Bangladesh, in their batting order, their captain, Litton Das, was the hero in the last game, as he scored a classy 76. Shamim Hossain and Tawhid Hridoy also played useful knocks that helped Bangladesh get to an above-par total on a slow wicket in the last game. Parvez Hossain Emon, the left-handed opener, has had two contrasting games, as he scored a quickfire 38 in the 1st game but then failed to open his account in the last one. On the bowling front, Bangladesh had a complete bowling performance in the last game, as each of the bowlers who bowled in that game got a wicket. Shoriful Islam started the bowling innings in some style as he picked up two in the powerplay. The rest of the bowlers followed suit, as Mohammad Saifuddin, too, finished with two wickets to his name, and the spin duo of Rishad Hossain and Mehidy Hasan Miraz shared 4 wickets between them as Bangladesh bundled out the Sri Lankan batting for 94. Now coming to this game, it will be interesting to see the surface that will be offered in Colombo, which might play a role in deciding the flow of the game. Bangladesh eyes an historic away series win, whereas Sri Lanka will look to add a home series win. So will Bangladesh create history? Or will the hosts reignite the winning feeling from the 1st game? We shall find out.
